body: **2026-11-08T20-32-52-wrap** — version census 0.2.0: the «deferred to 0.2.0; technology not chosen» frontend stub in §1, §5, §6, §7 and the keys wcag-criteria-mapping, structured-violation-json-schema, focus-management-test-harness, contrast-verification-harness became N/A (no web or graphical frontend), with the terminal fleet console (matrix#v2-14) taking its a11y scope at «Fleet a11y verification» and §5 naming the console's keyboard reach as that entry's; the P6 cli mirror says the console reuses `viola list`'s caption order. This is the stub this chunk's «surface section» replaces: the N/A overviews in the rows file come from it, and the console's surface must keep the board's captions and slot order.

**2026-10-16T14-58-10-wrap** — the web entities, browser harness, ARIA and contrast left 0.1.0; the frontend was deferred to 0.2.0 with its technology not chosen, and only the terminal surfaces stand (CLI output discipline, the TUI boundary, the wheel case, the manual SR passes). This is where the stub came from. The tier `Standard (1)` was left for the founder to re-decide (kept at 2026-11-01-t02-46-44-wrap). A new interactive console surface may reopen that tier question.

**2026-10-16-remove-the-browser-leg** — the browser a11y leg left. The cli and tui cases became nextest cases in the `test` job's `coverage` suite under `gate --require coverage,doctest`, with no a11y artifact, stage, budget, second driver or `suite` value of their own. The obs `ui` process was removed, leaving the `process` enum `run · hook · mcp · cli`. This is the origin of decision/a11y-runs-in-existing-test-suites, decision/no-separate-a11y-driver, decision/no-own-a11y-artifact and decision/no-a11y-performance-budget. Two things follow for this chunk: its keystroke driver must be an ordinary nextest case in `coverage`, never a new driver or suite value; and the «own diagnostics role» must reckon with `ui` having been removed from the process enum, not with `ui` as a live role.

**2026-09-24-diagnostics-plane** — the `a11y-violation` row was ruled not a product `event` value: a harness-only row, with the shipped `ObsEvent` and `diag-line.v1.json` enum carrying none. Precedent for this chunk's obs event catalog rows for the console role: a11y adds no product event of its own.

**2026-09-24-quality-gates** — the CLI output-discipline tests report under the CI `test` job's single instrumented `coverage` suite, gated by `gate --require coverage,doctest` (locally under `nextest-integration` / `nextest-e2e`), with failures only in `suites[].failures[]`. This is the source of decision/a11y-cases-inside-coverage-suite and decision/a11y-inside-existing-suites, and the console's keystroke cases land there.

**2026-09-24-supply-chain-and-workflow-gates** — `ci.yml` is the one push/PR workflow and the scheduled `nightly.yml` carries no a11y step (decision/a11y-ci-github-actions). This chunk's carry `cry-h6vzhlce` (the RUSTSEC chrono ignore in `deny.toml`) touches the nightly advisories run that this entry keeps a11y out of.

**2026-11-05-linux-only-code-and-ci** — this marker has several entries. They put the a11y cases on the one `ubuntu-latest` leg inside `coverage`, with `scripts/agent-run.sh run` the only runner. The TUI boundary is hosted on openpty alone, each of the three boundary clauses its own nextest case. They added the Linux-only platform line (decision/linux-only: «the 0.2.0 window features on Hyprland»). They made the manual SR pass Orca alone, the tui pairing Orca + foot on Hyprland and founder-owned. The cli SGR checks lost their Windows arms. The console's PTY driver, platform and SR pairing build on these.

**2026-11-06-version-done-check** — the cli checks are now `std::process::Command` with literal pins (trycmd and assert_cmd retired), and §8 says every fixed CLI string is pinned by a literal. The tui boundary driver moved to portable-pty `=0.9.0`, which a11y inherits and never re-pins. These are the sources of decision/cli-a11y-by-literal-tests, decision/tui-boundary-driver-pin and decision/fixed-cli-strings-pinned. The keystroke driver's PTY dependency must sit on that workspace pin, any new terminal-drawing or terminal-reading dependency is a fork, and the console's fixed strings need literal pins.

**2026-10-17-cli-output-discipline** — built the colour layer: bold NAME, amber only on `DIALOG`, dim on stale rows, each state carried by its word. The decision reads `NO_COLOR` (empty included), `TERM`, `COLORTERM` and whether stdout is a TTY, applies none under `--json` or a passthrough role, and picks a truecolor / 256 / 16 depth. A narrow terminal cuts an unwrapped NAME with `...`, the width from `viola_pty::host_size()`. Built the `--help` group labels over the served verbs. These are the sources of decision/colour-decision-inputs, decision/sgr-beside-its-word, decision/no-sgr-off-terminal, decision/unwrapped-name-truncation and contract/cli-help/*. A colour-drawing console frame must follow the same inputs and the word-beside-SGR rule, and a console start verb or flag joins the `--help` groups.

**2026-10-20-t06-58-31-wrap** — the founder ratified the `--help` served-verbs-only rows and `viola_pty::host_size()` as the board's cut-width source. A width source that already stands, relevant to the quarter-screen frame's size reading and its degrade rule.

**2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list** — the board's structure as built is BAY line → caption row → wrapped rows, with the `CAPTION` literal pinned by `list_human_board_is_the_literal_rows`, and there is no SGR on the board. This is the origin of the structural-equivalents rows the console's surface section extends.

**2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board** — added the `-- UNWRAPPED - READ-ONLY --` separator and unwrapped rows (NAME through `escape_row`), and the one 5 s `claude agents --json` read, which fails open and whose bound falls on viola's child. These are the structural carrier and the «agents read» bound that the time-bound rows list.

**2026-11-22-lineage-registry** — changed three rows: decision/terminal-structural-equivalents and decision/cli-structural-landmark-equivalents now add the `-- LINKS --` separator and the plain-space NAME indent of tree depth, and contract/viola-list-board/order became a tree plus the LINKS block. These are the exact rows the console's cli / tui landmarks entry extends. Each structural-carrier addition was a founder fork (F4, F5).

**2026-11-12T03-23-49-rows** — the masters became rows, each verified against the code, with twin areas (for example `1-a11y-scope-summary` / `a11y-scope-summary`). This explains the twin and duplicate rows in the rows file (for example decision/static-linear-output, decision/linear-static-output, decision/linear-static-cli-output and decision/no-spinners). A redraw exception has to be reconciled across every twin.

**2026-11-22T17-29-41Z-wrap** — this wrap named exceptions on zero-bytes and boundary rows rather than generalising them: `~ decision/portable-pty-outer-pty-driver` (except: the checks hold from the child's start), `~ decision/zero-viola-bytes-on-the-terminal`, `~ decision/wheel-ignores-terminal-events` and `~ contract/tui-passthrough/own-bytes` (the automatic-verify lines before the child). It added `+ decision/compiled-shapes-over-signatures` and paste write to both time-bound rows. This is the closest precedent for the redraw-ban reconciliation: each exception is narrow, named on the row's `except`, and decided by the operator.

**2026-11-24-adopt-s-resume-folder** — `~ decision/wheel-ignores-terminal-events` gained a second named exception (adopt's not-resumed pair after the child ends), and `~ contract/cli-refusal/unable-line` and `~ contract/cli-fixed-message/form` moved to «three own refusals». More precedent that an exception is named per surface on the row and that each new fixed-message refusal is added to the closed lists.

**2026-11-20-a-new-cli-version-stamped-automatically** — `~ contract/tui-passthrough/human-keystrokes`, `~ contract/tui-passthrough/viola-terminal-bytes` and `~ decision/human-keystrokes-never-blocked` gained the one named exception (the start's verify window, before the child). It was ratified at 2026-11-22T17-29-41Z-wrap. Another precedent for a narrow, named exception to a terminal-bytes promise.

**2026-11-17-standing-live-rig** — `~ decision/no-screen-content-parsing` gained its first `except`: a test-only rig that reads the vendor screen only as closed words, its raw frames kept local and gitignored. Precedent and constraint for this chunk's keystroke driver, which must read state and never screen bytes.

**2026-11-21-key-after-a-resize** — the latest form of `~ decision/no-screen-content-parsing` except: «the test-only rig reads closed words, never text: trust selector's place, input box empty, holds-text or absent, modals, box-row cell attributes before any send or after a turn end, send or KR resize». It was ratified at 2026-11-22T17-29-41Z-wrap. The row's except is a closed list that grows a member at a time; a console test driver reading anything screen-derived would be another named member, which is a fork.

**2026-11-13-verify-readiness-on-the-input-box** — `~ decision/no-screen-content-parsing` rule: parsing only for compiled signatures, the prompt row only for its opening char. It was ratified at 2026-11-27T19-07-11Z-wrap. With 2026-11-20-a-quoted-modal-never-blocks-a-send (the compiled shapes added), this is the rule's current text that the console driver's state-not-screen design must respect.

**2026-10-07-send-waits-out-the-paste-hint** — the new outer-PTY case is sequenced on the wrapper's lines and the `wheel` record, never a timer, and its limit of proof is stated. This is the origin of decision/boundary-tests-sequenced-on-records: the console's keystroke driver must sequence on log records or the state read, never on sleeps, inside the 20 s lint.

**2026-10-04-the-wheel** — set the closed list of non-editing terminal input (focus, mouse, terminal replies), with the boundary case run step-wise behind receipts. The console's own keys and the resize to a quarter screen meet this boundary's notion of what counts as editing.

**2026-11-18-session-folder-trusted-by-viola** — `~ decision/run-diagnostics-off-terminal`: `run`'s diagnostics go to `diagnostics/`, never the terminal, its trust word one `trust-record` line there. The same marker added the start's Claude config lock wait to `~ decision/time-bounds-never-on-human` and `~ decision/time-bounds-fall-on-the-driver`. This is a precedent for the console's own diagnostics role: diagnostics go to the log, never the console's terminal.

**2026-11-24-viola-adopt** — `~ contract/log-identity/process` (`process:"run"` for a `viola adopt` start), `~ contract/cli-refusal/unable-line`, `~ decision/strict-modes-refusal-before-any-write`, `~ contract/cli-fixed-message/form` and `~ contract/tui-passthrough/entry`. The same marker's later wrap set both time-bound rows' «Eight» lead to standing. Precedent for a new process or verb: each closed list (process tags, strict-modes verbs, fixed-message refusals) names the newcomer. The console's diagnostics role extends contract/log-identity/process.

**2026-11-24-viola-up** — added `+ contract/viola-up-output/instance-line`, a new human output surface given its own row. The operator's fork F1 settled that the time-bound rows hold «Eight», with `+ decision/open-live-wait-bound`, `+ decision/window-wait-bound` and `+ decision/hyprctl-read-deadline` as rows of their own. `~ contract/cli-exit-codes/21` gained `viola up`. A console bound (a redraw tick, a key read, a state poll) would take its own row, not join the lists.

**2026-11-24-viola-focus** — `~ decision/strict-modes-refusal-before-any-write` and `~ contract/cli-exit-codes/21` gained `viola focus`, a human-only Hyprland command. The ratification at 2026-11-24T17-14-08Z-wrap fixed the F1 rule: «a later bound a row only where it is new on a new bearer». This is the nearest precedent for a human-only window-side verb such as the console's start verb, and the rule for whether its bounds take rows.

**2026-11-22-epoch-4-cleanup** — `+ decision/start-verify-stop-grace-off-the-human`: the two time-bound lists are full at their bound, so the operator's ruling lands a new bound as a row of its own. Decides where any console time bound goes.

**2026-11-24-switching-a-session-s-model-and-effort** — added `+ contract/viola-switch-output/result-line` (a new verb's output-discipline row) and `+ decision/respawn-reap-bound` (its bound as a row of its own), and changed exit 10 and decision/send-refused-while-human-typing to name `switch`. Another precedent for how a new human surface enters the plan row by row.

**2026-11-14-budget-gate-removed** — `~ decision/time-bounds-fall-on-the-driver`, `~ decision/time-bounds-never-on-human` and `~ decision/state-carried-by-printed-word` (budget-paused dropped from the board's state words). These rows carry the board's state words, which a console view would reuse. Not later reversed.

**2026-10-10-viola-revive** — a passed `viola revive` joined the passthrough and the zero-SGR list, and its exit-1 refusals took the fixed `unable:` / `hint:` form. This is the source of the «passed `viola revive`» member of decision/no-sgr-in-plain-modes and decision/no-sgr-off-terminal. Precedent for how a new start path enters the no-SGR and refusal-form lists.

**2026-10-26-explicit-session-links** — built the `handoff:` help row (`handoff:  link, unlink` between `wheel:` and `setup:`, contract/cli-help/handoff-row) and added the link verbs' result lines to the literal-pinned strings. A console start verb in `--help` would change contract/cli-help/group-labels and usage-line, which are held by `help_is_the_grouped_verb_table` and `help_lists_only_served_verbs`.

**2026-10-17-optional-plugin-install** — `plugin install` built as one entry in `setup:`, with a bare `plugin` unserved (contract/cli-help/served-verbs-only). The served-verbs-only rule any console verb must follow in `--help`.

**2026-10-31-sanitised-error-surfaces** — `unknown`'s detail is a code word or nothing (contract/cli-refusal/unknown-refusal, decision/refusal-ends-with-hint except). The census `error_bodies_each_name_a_writer_and_a_witness_that_stand` was added (decision/error-bodies-have-writer-and-witness). Any console refusal or error body must have a named writer and a witness in `tests/contract_error_bodies.rs`.

**2026-10-31-exit-cause-code-catalogue** — added `no_two_codes_share_a_hint`, `no_hint_names_release` and the exit-cause table `tests/cross_exit_causes.rs` (guards of decision/one-hint-per-code and decision/no-hint-names-release). New console refusal hints fall under these catalogue checks.

**2026-11-25-placing-without-moving-the-view** — `~ contract/cli-fixed-message/form` gained `viola verify`'s untrusted-folder refusal. This is the row's current closed list, which a console start's fixed-message refusal would extend.

**2026-09-28-mutation-testing-to-the-epoch-boundary** — the CLI output-discipline invariants are covered by the epoch-boundary mutation audit (`run --mutants`), not by a per-chunk gate. The scaffold's invariants meet mutation only at the Epoch 6 boundary, and this phase runs no mutation.

Builds the fleet console's scaffold: its own surface section in the masters (beside Surface: cli, with the cli / tui landmarks), replacing the 0.1.0 stub deferred to 0.2.0, and the minimal code behind it.
Fixes the console's quarter-screen layout and smallest whole size, and a frame that stays whole there and degrades by a named rule below it.
Reconciles the redraw bans with an interactive console: an exception named for the console's own surface only, never generalised (provisional, the operator's fork).
Adds a test-only keystroke driver feeding the console keys through its own pseudo-terminal under a test-owned home, asserting on the console's state or log lines, never screen bytes; and the console's own diagnostics role reachable through the logs command.
Folds two carries: re-reads the chrono advisory RUSTSEC-2026-0543 and its ignore; restructures the per-paste probe step and the relied-row count / stamped-set table to one source.

body: The console's surface section: a new interactive terminal surface written beside the cli and tui surfaces, with its own structural landmark equivalents; rows owed to the fleet view (columns) and console actions (keys) named as owed, not built.

Redraw-ban reconciliation: the rows banning spinners, in-place rewrites and cursor-moving status and requiring linear static output reach the console only through an exception named for the console's own surface; the ban stands unchanged for every CLI verb.

The console as keyboard-interactive: the rules that the CLI takes no interactive input and is not keyboard-interactive get a carve-out for the console surface alone; the scaffold's own keys are quit and whatever the frame needs, no verb.
The keystroke test driver asserts on the console's state (a structured read exposed for tests) or its log lines, never on screen bytes; the ban on screen-content parsing binds its assertions.

The driver owns its pseudo-terminal under a test-owned home, over the fake agent and fixtures as the contract; no real terminal, no real claude, nothing of the operator's real home; each console test bounded under the 20 s lint.
Which pseudo-terminal library drives the console in tests, against the pinned outer-PTY boundary driver; any new dependency that draws or reads a terminal is the operator's fork.
Quarter-screen layout: the frame stays whole at the smallest size the layout fixes and degrades below it by a named rule, the way NAME truncation on a narrow terminal is ruled.
The frame's own bytes: control characters escaped in anything it prints, no SGR without a colour-capable terminal, any colour only a second cue beside its word, failure words never coloured.

The console's diagnostics role: structured logs under its own role beside run, hook, mcp and ui, reachable through the logs command, never written to the console's terminal; log identity tags (process, service_name) carry it; the obs event catalog's rows for it.
The console's start verb or flag and its name (the operator's fork): if a verb or flag is added, the help listing of served verbs, its usage line and group labels reach it.
Any fixed string the scaffold prints (frame caption, quit hint) comes from design copy and is pinned by literal; a refusal it raises follows the unable line, reason code and hint layout.
Time bounds never fall on the human at the console: the scaffold imposes no time limit on the user; bounds fall on the test driver only.
The console's a11y checks run as literal / state assertions inside the existing suites, failing as nextest failures, with no skips and no retries, under the GitHub Actions gate.

Carry cry-h6vzhlce: the chrono unmaintained advisory re-read; an upgrade found, the ignore leaves; none, the ignore stands one more epoch on the operator's word, its reason line still saying it is re-read at each boundary.

Restructure invariant for carry cry-boujwuyr: framing_turns' per-paste probes moved into one step function and send_through's guarded section looked at, the relied-row count taken from one source and the stamped-set table held once; what each does stays as it is, held by the existing tests over them.
No crate without a real consumer and a test; every console layer agent-runnable headless over the fake agent and fixtures.

body_fields.convention: each new test fails as a nextest failure inside the existing suites and coverage run, no skips, no retries, zero flakiness
each new log line goes to the diagnostics log under its role with its identity tags, never to a terminal
each new fixed CLI string is taken from design copy and pinned by a literal test

body: The output contracts of individual verbs (the list board and its caption, revive, link and unlink, wait, verify, switch, up, plugin install): the scaffold prints none of them and changes none.
The socket and IPC refusal contracts (frame-verb refusals, hook calls, MCP frame tools, instance-unreachable details, start-against-holder refusals): the scaffold opens no instance channel.
The critical paths for send readback, dialog answer and taking the wheel, and the send-refused-while-typing rule: these belong to the console actions entry.
The board colour rows (amber on DIALOG, bold NAME, dim stale rows): the fleet rows inside the frame are the fleet console view's.
The compositor time bounds (each compositor read, window step wait, live open wait, respawn reap): the chunk opens or moves no window and dispatches nothing to the compositor.
The manual Orca and manual keyboard passes and their screen-reader targets: the SC checks over the finished console are the fleet a11y verification entry's.
The absences of a web or graphical frontend, a touch surface, a rendered page and internationalisation: the console is a terminal surface and touches none of them.
The viola run TUI passthrough contracts (human keystrokes, focus/mouse/resize sequences, vendor content, vt100 feed panic): the console is its own process, not the wrapped claude terminal.

**2026-09-24-diagnostics-plane** (diagnostics roots, config key, diag schemas, v exception) — set every role's codes-only log to its own home-level role file (`run-`/`hook-`/`mcp`/`ui-`/`cli-`), content detail only in the instance `detail-<role>.ndjson`, `diagnostics_level` the sole level source, process-log lines carrying no `v`. The console's «own diagnostics role» extends exactly this register (rows decision/codes-only-process-logs, contract/diagnostics-role-files/*, contract/diag-line/format); the `ui-` file named here was later cut (n=9).

**2026-09-24-log-redaction-and-never-log-floor** — anyhow stays in the root bin (`main`, dispatch, the catch-site reporter `viola::obs::report_internal_error`), context chains only in the owner-only detail file, never a role line, stdout or stderr. A new console process role inherits this catch-site rule (rows decision/error-chain-to-diagnostics-only, decision/anyhow-only-in-bin).

**2026-09-24-observability-gates** — added the workspace `print_stdout`/`print_stderr`/`dbg_macro` bans, `disallowed-macros` on the tracing level macros (`obs_event!` the one emitter) and the lint probes. A console that draws to a terminal must write through sanctioned writers, never print macros (rows decision/clippy-print-and-macro-bans, decision/no-print-macros, decision/obs-event-only-emitter).

**2026-09-24-supply-chain-and-workflow-gates** — the sole-root tokio ban per sync crate (`deny-sync.toml`, `scripts/sync-crates.txt`) and the four-family `deny.toml` (advisories, licences, sources, C/telemetry/feature bans). Any terminal-drawing or key-reading dependency the scaffold proposes (his fork) must pass these bans and keep the sync graph tokio-free (rows decision/cargo-deny-dependency-policy, decision/sync-crates-tokio-free).

**2026-09-24-three-os-ci-headless-harness-skeleton** (test-only crate, bins, env vars, paths) — Module Boundaries gained «each product crate is created by its first consumer», and the test-only `viola-e2e`/`viola-harness`/`AGENT_RUN_` prefix were registered. Binds the scope's «no crate without a real consumer and a test» and where a keystroke test driver and its env knobs may live (rows decision/cargo-workspace-flat-crates, decision/harness-env-var-prefix).

**2026-09-28-hook-perf-gate** (the second fake-agent test seam `FAKE_AGENT_HOOK_PANIC`) — a new unprefixed test seam was a boundary widening ratified by the founder, read only under `cfg(feature = "fake-agent")`. Precedent: if the keystroke driver needs a product-side test seam to expose console state, that seam is a widening needing his word (rows decision/test-seams-not-configuration, decision/env-var-viola-prefix).

**2026-09-28-cli-output-tokens** — clap built without `color` (its anstream route read CLICOLOR/NO_COLOR/TERM/COLORTERM/CI) and `src/human.rs` named the root bin's one human writer. The console must not bring a crate that re-opens an env-reading colour route, and its human output belongs to the human module (rows decision/clap-without-color-feature, decision/single-human-writer).

**2026-10-04-wait-and-last** (the cli role's one internal-error printer) — `role_of` files every first word but `run`, `hook` and a leading flag under `cli`, and the `main` catch site prints the internal-error line once. A console verb gets a role through `role_of`; whether it is `cli` (prints the line) or a silent role like `run`/`mcp` (n=17, n=20) is a choice this chunk must make.

**2026-10-16T14-58-10-wrap** (0.1.0 is a pure CLI; the frontend moves to 0.2.0) — retired the view-only loopback GUI: no `ui` subcommand, no `ui-<port>` role file, no `UiError`, no `viola-ui` crate; four interfaces from one binary; the masters' GUI sections cut to a «deferred to 0.2.0, technology not chosen» stub. This is the stub the scaffold's surface section replaces, and it answers the scope's question «whether `ui` already is that role»: the `ui` role was removed (rows decision/four-interfaces-one-binary, overview/project-intent).

**2026-11-08T20-32-52-wrap** (version census 0.2.0) — [Real-time Strategy], [GUI Control Scope], GUI contracts and Product type now say: no web or graphical frontend; the view beyond `viola list` is the keyboard-driven terminal fleet console tiled on Hyprland, owed by «Console scaffold», «Fleet console view» and «Console actions»; the console's contracts owed by «Console scaffold». The direct mandate for this chunk's surface section and the absence rows it must not breach (decision/terminal-fleet-console, absence/graphical-frontend, absence/graphical-interface, absence/web-or-graphical-frontend).

**2026-10-17-cli-output-discipline** — the colour layer `src/human/style.rs` reads `NO_COLOR`/`TERM`/`COLORTERM` (read, never set, deciding only SGR bytes), ratified by the founder as a widening, with the precedent that any further environment read or a colour fact reaching a control needs its own ratification. A console reading `TERM`, sizes or other terminal env (e.g. `COLUMNS`, not read today) is that kind of widening (rows decision/colour-env-decides-only-sgr, contract/human-output-colour-env/*, decision/no-environment-configuration).

**2026-10-13-epoch-4-cleanup** (send and human split by phase) — the `human` module root over `src/human/` (mirror, escape, board, wait, verbs, hints) is the root bin's only human writer, split as a pure move under 800 code lines. The console's drawing and its later `unable` lines sit beside this module, and the cleanup precedent governs the carried M1/M3 refactors (row decision/single-human-writer).

**2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers** (the Tokio client and viola-channel's tree-form ban; the MCP tools' contract) — Tokio confined to `viola-mcp` (and `viola-channel`'s feature), `role_of` excludes `mcp` from `cli` and `Role::Mcp` never prints the internal-error line. A console process runs on std threads unless it is ruled otherwise, and its role mapping follows this precedent (rows decision/hybrid-concurrency, decision/tokio-only-in-mcp-crate, decision/tokio-containment, decision/viola-channel-tokio-free-by-default).

**2026-10-10-budget-governor** (the instance check before any log, on both arms) — measured that opening a log sets an existing home to 0700, so a check after it cannot refuse a widened home; refused checks write no line. The console's own role log must open only after its strict-modes check (rows decision/strict-check-before-log-open, decision/refused-check-writes-no-line).

**2026-10-26-home-and-code-bearing-file-integrity** — every checked entry point runs its strict-modes/instance check before any log; `open_role_file`/`write_detail` run `check_diagnostics` (symlink refused, read rule) before narrowing; the read rule defined. Quarter-screen layout: the frame stays whole at a quarter of the screen and at its smallest size, and degrades by a named rule below it; the scaffold opens or moves no window and the tiled window is the view entry's.

Redraw-ban reconciliation: the rows that ban redraw on the CLI's surfaces, the rule that run writes only the child's output to the terminal, and the colour rules (clap without colour, colour variables deciding only SGR output) reach the console only through an exception named for its own surface; the rule stays as it is for every other surface — a boundary widening, the founder's fork.

Human output writing: the console's drawing must go through the one human writer of the root bin, under the print and dbg macro bans and the clippy deny-warnings gate; short-lived CLI verbs' stderr allowance does not cover a long-lived console.

A new dependency that draws or reads a terminal is the founder's fork; any one taken must pass the cargo-deny policy (licence allowlist, crates.io sources only, no C-building crates, banned features, no telemetry crates), be pinned once in the workspace's dependency table, and keep the sync crates tokio-free with Tokio only inside mcp.

The console is a process, never a daemon: no daemon, no listening network port, no polling; the disk stays the shared truth.

The keystroke test driver: test-only, kept out of release builds and product builds behind the test-support feature, driving only the scaffold's own keys (quit and what the frame needs) through its own pseudo-terminal; it asserts on the console's structured state or its log lines, never on screen bytes.

The console's state read for tests: a structured read the console exposes for tests is a test seam, never a configuration channel; any seam variable carries the test-harness or fake-agent seam prefix, never the VIOLA_ product namespace, and is never read by the product otherwise.

Console tests run over the fake agent and fixtures as the contract (headless agent verification first): no live claude, no real terminal key, no compositor dispatch, nothing read of the operator's real home; each under a test-owned viola home and bounded under the 20 s lint and the root tests' one shared wait bound.

body: A new process role for the console: one diagnostics log file per process role, the role list and its count wherever a row pins it, the process field's closed values, and the role taken from argv before clap.

The console role's diagnostics file paths and home resolution: owner-only file and directory modes, the home strict-modes check before diagnostics init, and whether its lines are home-level (path-free, content-free) or instance-scoped, given the instance source fixed per role.
The harness logs command reaching the console's role file: its merged sources, filters, output record envelope and torn-line handling.

The obs event catalog rows for the console process: its process-start and process-exit lines with service name and version from the compiled constants, pid and os, its closed exit detail codes, and corr by event.

The interactive terminal interface absence (prompt, TUI or pager) and the redraw-ban reconciliation: the console becomes an interactive surface by a named exception for its own surface, the rule never widened for other CLI surfaces.

Stdout and stderr by role for the console: the console's terminal carries its frame and no telemetry, no ANSI codes and no screen content in diagnostics lines, logs to its file sink only, and its error output keeps the fixed-message rule.
Keys typed into the console are never logged and no telemetry is taken from screen content; the keystroke driver asserts on the console's structured state or its log lines, never on screen bytes.

Panic capture in the console role: panic hook installed first and silent on stderr, one single-line panic record, exit decided at the console's catch site, panic = unwind kept, and a panic outcome by role entry for the console.

Diagnostics init order for the console: panic hook, home tree check, then log open before the role's work; a refused or failed log open discards lines; level from config only, never from the environment.

Any new dependency that draws or reads a terminal: obs dependencies Tokio-free and C-free, passing cargo deny, not on the banned telemetry and logging list, its log target off among third-party targets.

The chrono advisory carry: RUSTSEC-2026-0543 re-read at the boundary, the ignore leaving with a safe upgrade or standing one more epoch with its reason line; a cargo deny failure is a failure, and chrono stays the direct timestamp dependency for millisecond UTC timestamps.

The restructure's invariant: the framing-turns per-paste probes folded into one step function, the send-through guarded section only looked at, the relied-row count read from one source and the stamped-set table held once — what each does stays as it is, held by the existing send-path log-event, send-refused detail and confirm-window checks and the relied-row tests.

Any console code that logs or declares spans goes through the obs_event macro with a closed event enum and the default-deny field allow-list, no raw tracing macros, instrument skipping all arguments, static low-cardinality span names, and no print macros in product paths.

Console tests run under a test-owned home and their own pseudo-terminal, bounded under the 20 s lint, against the fake agent and fixtures only; no live start, no real claude, no real terminal or compositor, no read of the operator's real homes.
The console scaffold makes no hot-path instrumentation of its redraw loop: no info logging in hot loops and no line per redraw or keystroke.
The console's start verb or flag and its name (his fork): the CLI process-log file the verb writes, and its process-exit detail codes on refusal.

each new diagnostics line carries only the fixed line fields and is additive to the log schema, never renaming a frozen field
each new integration or E2E test that runs a process has its emitted lines schema-checked and its home under the one integration-test root, kept until the gates run
each new log line names no path, pid, typed content or secret in a home-level file; content-bearing records go to the instance detail file only
each new obs code path is mutation-tested like product code, and the zero-panics and schema gates still read every role file
each new test waits on log lines or state by condition, never by sleep

body: A new interactive console process and surface: the console is a new CLI surface with its own start verb or flag, so the CLI input trust boundary and the checks a CLI verb owes before it reads the home (home resolution order through --home and VIOLA_DIR, owner-only home, strict-modes check before any read) bind its start.
The console's start checks the home tree before its diagnostics log opens; a refused diagnostics open writes nowhere, and a diagnostics file failing strict modes fails open.

Redraw-ban reconciliation: any redraw allowance is an exception named for the console's own surface, never a widened or switchable control; no config, env var or flag turns a control off, and no width or colour override env is introduced.

The console's frame is human-mode terminal output: C0/C1 control characters in any text it draws are escaped, terminal colour facts choose SGR only and colour environment variables are only compared, and error messages it shows are fixed, interpolating no paths, ids or upstream text.

The console reads keystrokes from its terminal: every product reader stays bounded or is named in the bounded-readers census, and a key read is input checked at the seam, never treated as a command from upstream text.

The console's own diagnostics role: its log files are owner-only and keep their modes over rotation, user content goes only to diagnostics, full error detail only to diagnostics, and CLAUDE values and messaging secrets are never logged.

The console's process is a new product error writer and a new source of panics: every error writer is named, the zero-panics gate's single exemption is not widened, and stderr honours the never-log floor.

A state read the console exposes for tests is a test seam: it lives only under the fake-agent feature, is compiled out of release, the release build refuses test-only binaries and features, and test-support stays a development-only dependency.

The keystroke test driver keys only into its own pseudo-terminal under a test-owned home, runs no real claude, reads nothing of the operator's real Claude home or viola home, removes only directories it created, and stays bounded under the 20 s test lint.

Any new dependency that draws or reads a terminal: crates.io only, exact pin, licence on the closed allow list, no C-building crate, no tokio in the sync crates, within the minimum supported Rust version, and passing the cargo-deny gate on the root graph.

The chrono advisory carry: the RUSTSEC-2026-0543 ignore is admitted only on the advisory-ignore grounds and stays on the closed ignore list only while no safe upgrade exists; an upgrade removes the ignore with it, and the reason line keeps saying it is re-read at each epoch boundary.

A new log role and any new environment read or seam the console adds owes its log entry, and its log lines carry no paths, pids or ids in refusals.
The console writes nothing under the Claude home and sends no key to a real terminal, opens or moves no window and dispatches nothing to the compositor in this chunk.

body: The console's own diagnostics role: structured JSON process logs written under a new role beside run, hook, mcp and ui, reachable through the logs command; the obs event catalog rows for its events; the roles' list and its count wherever a row or test pins it.

The console's process log lines follow the process log line fields (timestamp, level, process, event, corr, target, message, null encoding), codes-only role logs with detail apart, and the diagnostics schema conformance check over them.
The console's diagnostics files are private: owner-only modes, umask-independent, and they carry no secrets.

The keystroke test driver asserts on the console's state (a structured read exposed for tests, or its log lines) and never on rendered screen bytes: the no-screen-parsing and E2E-asserts-on-events rules, and test waits keyed on logged events rather than sleeps or retries.
The driver feeds keys through a real pseudo-terminal of its own (real openpty in integration tests, outer PTY reader drained on its own thread, child exit read on the process handle, never on EOF).

Every console test runs under a test-owned home and its own pseudo-terminal, reads nothing of the host's claude sessions or viola home, drops inherited session environment, and is bounded under the 20 s per-test kill line.
The console scaffold is agent-runnable headless over the fake agent and its recorded fixtures as the contract; no real claude CLI, no live window, compositor or real terminal in any test.
The test-only state read the console exposes for the driver stays test-only: it must not reach the release build, which carries viola only.
Where the keystroke driver and any test-only crate code live: the single test-only workspace member and tokio test code confined to the E2E crate; no new crate without a real consumer and a test.

Redraw-ban reconciliation: the rows banning spinners, in-place rewrites and cursor-moving status and the no-SGR / no-escape-without-a-terminal rules for CLI human output get an exception named for the console's surface alone; the CLI verbs keep them unchanged.
Text the console's frame draws escapes control characters, as human-mode output does.

The quarter-screen layout: the frame stays whole at its smallest fixed size and degrades by a named rule below it, proved through the driver's state read after a resize (a key after a resize waits for the new size).
The console's start verb or flag is a new CLI surface: tested as a subprocess, listed in the grouped verb table of viola --help, its human output pinned by literals.
Any new dependency that draws or reads a terminal passes the cargo-deny gate: tokio and C-crate bans, tokio-free sync crates that compile alone, one version source per tool, MSRV floor.

every new test waits on logged events, never sleeps, never retries, never shares mutable state and runs in parallel
every new test oracle is a literal and asserts on the contract, never on Debug strings or fixture internals
every new test function follows the test naming rule, and a new root integration binary is prefixed by its surface and selected by its layer filterset
every new OS-gated test is registered with its reason in the binary's root file
every new test input is synthetic, carries the canary and passes the fixture hygiene walk
every new log line carries the process log line fields and its event's corr
new code stays within the comprehensive-tier coverage floors, child viola processes counted
